pr.title: Don't call closure_by_move_body_def_id on FnOnce async closures in MIR validation
pr.description:
Refactors the check in #129847 to not unncessarily call the `closure_by_move_body_def_id` query for async closures that don't *need* a by-move body.

Fixes #130167
pr.author: compiler-errors

processing.reason: The PR fixes a compiler-internal MIR-validation ICE (a released `coroutine_by_move_body_def_id` query reads a stolen `Body`), not a source-level value transformation. The historical "incorrect" behavior is an over-broad query gate that panics while compiling an `async FnOnce` closure; it has no defined runtime execution whose returned value differs from the corrected behavior. Any ordinary Rust function pair that passed Miri on both sides would necessarily behave identically on this input, and encoding the compiler's internal `needs_coroutine_by_move_body_def_id` boolean as a hand-written return value would manufacture an unrelated artificial difference rather than model a historical source-to-source transformation. The added regression test is `//@ build-pass`, confirming that the only observable difference is successful compilation versus a compiler panic, which Miri cannot execute under the fixed modern compiler.

analysis.summary: The MIR Validator must not request a coroutine by-move body merely because a coroutine is a desugared closure with FnOnce closure kind. It must first use needs_coroutine_by_move_body_def_id so the coroutine_by_move_body_def_id query is invoked only for async closures that actually need a by-move body.
analysis.originalLogic: In compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/validate.rs, the TypeChecker selected a coroutine layout for a non-caller def_id based on whether the def_id was a desugared closure coroutine and whether its closure kind was FnOnce: `else if let Some(hir::CoroutineKind::Desugared(_, hir::CoroutineSource::Closure)) = self.tcx.coroutine_kind(def_id) && let ty::ClosureKind::FnOnce = args.as_coroutine().kind_ty().to_opt_closure_kind().unwrap() && self.caller_body.source.def_id() ...`. That path could then obtain the by-move body via coroutine_by_move_body_def_id. The needs_coroutine_by_move_body_def_id helper already existed and checked for a desugared closure coroutine (`if let Some(hir::CoroutineKind::Desugared(_, hir::CoroutineSource::Closure)) = self.coroutine_kind(def_id) && let ty::Coroutine(_, args) = self.type_of(def_id).instantiate_identity().kind()`).
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect validator behavior treated the coarse test “desugared closure coroutine + FnOnce closure kind” as sufficient proof that a by-move body exists, and consequently called coroutine_by_move_body_def_id for async closures that do not need a by-move body. For such a closure the by-move body query has no valid Body to read, producing `attempted to read from stolen value: rustc_middle::mir::Body` during validation. The corrected transformation replaces the coarse coroutine-kind test with `self.tcx.needs_coroutine_by_move_body_def_id(def_id)` before proceeding to the FnOnce check and by-move-body access; the helper signature is widened from LocalDefId to DefId so the Validator can call it.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust programs compiled with `#![feature(async_closure)]` that use an `async FnOnce` bound and an async closure expression, in a context that causes MIR shims and validation to run (for example passing the async closure to an async `call_once` function and driving the future with a block_on helper). The relevant compiler-state class is a coroutine whose kind is a desugared closure with FnOnce closure kind but for which `needs_coroutine_by_move_body_def_id` is false. A contrasting input for the same validator path is a coroutine/closure for which the needs predicate is true, so the by-move body query is legitimate.
analysis.trigger: MIR validation visits a coroutine def_id that is a desugared async closure with FnOnce closure kind, where the closure does not need a by-move body, and the old validator unconditionally reaches the coroutine_by_move_body_def_id query.
preconditions: The program contains an async closure used through a generic `async FnOnce` bound.
MIR validation runs while generating a MIR shim / monomorphizing, so the Validator is active on the closure's coroutine body.
The coroutine is a Desugared closure coroutine with FnOnce closure kind.
The coroutine does not need a by-move body, so the needs_coroutine_by_move_body_def_id predicate is false.
pitfalls: Do not assume that FnOnce closure kind alone means a by-move body exists or should be queried.
Do not replace `needs_coroutine_by_move_body_def_id(def_id)` with a plain `coroutine_kind(def_id)` check; that reintroduces the over-broad query.

The issue description says async closures that do not need a by-move body, while the added test comment describes async closures that are FnOnce; the precise invariant is the needs predicate, not merely FnOnce.
The old code also used the caller-body source def_id and FnOnce conditions; preserve those remaining conditions when changing only the coroutine-kind gate.
The fix changes the needs helper to accept DefId because validate.rs has a DefId, so LocalDefId-only call sites must pass `to_def_id()`.
This is a compiler ICE fix; do not describe the test as executed or the ICE as reproduced without a built compiler.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a build-pass UI test under tests/ui/async-await/async-closures, modeled on body-check-on-non-fnmut.rs: use `//@ aux-build:block-on.rs`, `//@ edition:2021`, `//@ build-pass`, enable `#![feature(async_closure)]`, define `async fn empty() {}`, a generic `pub async fn call_once<F: async FnOnce()>(f: F) { f().await; }`, and call `block_on::block_on(call_once(async || empty().await))`. The expected outcome is successful compilation without the stolen-Body panic. As a differential counterpart, compile an otherwise equivalent case whose needs_coroutine_by_move_body_def_id predicate is true so the legitimate by-move-body path still validates. Treat both as source-level test designs; no execution or reproduction is claimed here.
